business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Articles 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), in particular Articles 626-629 on articles of association, Article 632 on paid-up capital, Article 634 on minimum capital, Articles 716a-716b and 718 on board powers and representation, and Article 727 et seq. on audit requirements; supplemented by the Civil Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office; supervised by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office within the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (öffentliche Urkunde) containing the Articles of Association (Statuten), executed by a Swiss notary and filed in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG must have minimum statutory share capital of CHF 100,000. Before registration, at least CHF 50,000 must be actually paid in, with each share paid to at least 20% of its par value; the paid-in amount must be deposited in a blocked (escrow) bank account with a licensed Swiss bank and released for ordinary use only after Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
Pro Forma First Board Resolution of CH_AG.

RESOLVED: the share subscriptions set out in the signature pages are accepted, creating a share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 10,000 registered shares with a par value of CHF 10 each; the shares are fully paid into a blocked bank account, and the bank escrow confirmation is authorized for delivery to the Commercial Register; the registered office is fixed at the address in the articles of association; the following directors are appointed each with sole/joint signatory authority as stated in the public deed: [Name], [Name], [Name]; all directors and officers are authorized to complete registration, tax registration, and all licensing filings. This resolution is effective on notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Legal-Form Suffix Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) / Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the desired company name through Zefix and submit a name-clearance request to the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office. Verify that the name includes the mandatory suffix 'AG' or 'SA', is truthful and not misleading, and does not conflict with an existing registered company name or a prior trademark of a third party. Retain the written name-clearance confirmation for later notarial use.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Proposed Articles of Association (draft Statuten)
Passport copies of founders and directors
Declaration of permissible legal-form suffix
Optional trademark search report from the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for deception, lack of distinctiveness, or conflict with an existing entity, submit a revised name ranking with explanatory memorandum and, where necessary, a trademark consent letter; reapply to the same cantonal Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked (escrow) account in the name of the future AG with a licensed Swiss bank. Deposit at least the statutory minimum of CHF 50,000, or the higher amount specified in the articles, ensuring that each share is paid up to at least 20% of par value. Obtain an official bank confirmation that the amount is irrevocably at the company's free disposal immediately upon Commercial Register registration and remains blocked until then.
required_dossiers: Account opening application and beneficial-ownership forms
Notarized or certified identity documents of all subscribers
Draft Articles of Association
Source-of-funds declaration and AML/KYC responses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced KYC questions or refuses the escrow confirmation, provide supplementary source-of-wealth evidence and a sworn financial statement; alternatively, open the escrow account at another licensed Swiss bank and inform the notary before deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Public Deed Execution and Statutory Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name clearance, bank capital confirmation, final Articles of Association, directors' mandate acceptances, and identity documents. The notary verifies compliance with the Swiss Code of Obligations, authenticates the public deed of incorporation, and then issues the certified notarial deed with all annexes for Commercial Register submission.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all founders and directors
Name-clearance certificate
Bank capital payment confirmation
Final Articles of Association (Statuten)
Directors' mandate acceptance forms and signature sheets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies in the articles or capital confirmation, execute a supplementary correction deed, amend the statutory text by unanimous shareholder/board resolution, and have the corrected document notarized in the same session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register E-Filing and SHAB Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office / Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial public deed and annexes electronically through the Commercial Register Office's official e-filing channel. Pay the statistical registration fee and SHAB publication fee. Respond to any clarifications from the registrar; once registered, the AG acquires legal personality and the Commercial Register publishes the entry in SHAB with the company's name, seat, capital, and officers.
required_dossiers: Notarial public deed of incorporation
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Bank capital payment confirmation
Directors' appointments and authorized signature forms
Commercial Register application forms and fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency notice or third-party objection, supplement the requested documents within the statutory cure period or apply for administrative suspension; if formal refusal is issued, appeal to the competent cantonal administrative authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, AHV and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) / AHV Compensation Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the cantonal tax administration of the new company for corporate income tax and capital tax purposes using the UID issued after Commercial Register registration. Register with the Federal Tax Administration for value added tax if the annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, or voluntarily if desired. Register as employer with the cantonal AHV compensation office and with SUVA or a private accident insurer for occupational accident coverage.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract and UID confirmation
Articles of Association and effective management address evidence
Directors' identity and residence/work permits
Bank signatory list and corporate account confirmation
VAT registration form and AHV employer registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the canton challenges the effective seat, provide lease agreement, utility bills, attendance records, and board meeting minutes demonstrating Swiss administration; if VAT classification is disputed, submit an appeal within the statutory deadline to the Federal Tax Administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Premises Licensing and Bonded Warehouse Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG), Cantonal Alcohol and Public Economy Licensing Authority, Cantonal Labour and Fire Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for customs bonded warehouse authorization for wine and spirits storage and, where distilled spirits are held, a cantonal alcohol wholesale permit. The customs authority inspects the physical premises, inventory and excise suspension system, chamber security, seals, and warehouse organization. In parallel, obtain fire safety clearance, building occupancy authorization, and occupational workplace clearance before start of operations.
required_dossiers: Site plan, floor plan, and lease authorization for the warehouse
Bonded warehouse inventory and stock management protocol
Cantonal alcohol wholesale trade license application
Fire safety concept and structural load certificate
Environmental spill-containment and wastewater concept
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the customs or cantonal inspector reports deficiencies, implement the required security and inventory-control corrections, submit an interim response, and request a re-inspection; if the license is refused, use the cantonal administrative appeal or, for customs decisions, an appeal to the Federal Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS; Bundesamt für Zoll und Grenzsicherheit) together with the Cantonal Alcohol and Public Economy Licensing Authority and the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Bonded Warehouse Authorization (Zolllager-/Steuerlagerbewilligung) for Wine and Spirits, combined with a Cantonal Wholesale Alcohol Trade Permit and, where applicable, a Federal Alcohol Wholesale License for distilled spirits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the competent Cantonal Environmental Protection Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Preliminary environmental registration/screening is required for a bonded warehouse and spirits wholesale storage operation; a full environmental impact assessment (EIA) is only required if the installation meets or exceeds the thresholds of Annex I of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/EIE), particularly for very large ethanol or flammable-liquid storage, otherwise a simplified cantonal environmental review is performed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201) for effluents, the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) VOC and airborne emission limits, the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600) for waste and hazardous waste records, and the Ordinance on Protection against Major Accidents (Störfallverordnung, SR 814.012) for threshold quantities of ethanol and wine/spirit losses.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-prevention and civil-defense clearance from the Cantonal Fire Inspectorate (Feuerpolizei) and municipal building control, including a structural load certificate for racked wine and cask storage and an alcohol-spill containment plan; occupational safety approval under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG), administered with SUVA, covering emergency exits, ventilation, fire extinguishing systems, hazardous-material storage signage, and workplace health requirements before operational commencement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV; Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC; Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni – ACF), official portal https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT Main Division and Swiss Business Identification Number (UID) Register via the Federal Statistical Office portal https://www.uid.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity conducting taxable activities in Switzerland must file Swiss tax registration Form 701 (Anmeldung zur Mehrwertsteuer) with the ESTV, either on paper or via secure SwissLogin e-services, before commencing the taxable activity; the Federal Statistical Office then allocates a Swiss Business Identification Number (UID, format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX) which serves as the VAT ID; registration is effective from the date of economic activity commencement, and the cantonal tax authorities are notified separately for income and capital tax purposes if a permanent establishment exists, with the UID being the statutory reference in all VAT filings, invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG/Société Anonyme) is taxed at entity level on worldwide profits if statutorily resident in Switzerland, comprising Federal direct tax (statutory rate 8.5%) plus cantonal and communal profits and capital taxes; companies without a Swiss registered office are taxed at entity level only on Swiss-source profits attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment; no pass-through or transparent classification exists for VAT or corporate income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (i) VAT group taxation ('Organschaft' under Art. 77 MWSTG) covering financially, economically and organizationally integrated Swiss entities; (ii) voluntary VAT registration when annual taxable turnover is below the CHF 100,000 statutory threshold, permitting input VAT deduction; (iii) election between actual input VAT deduction and approved lump-sum/flat-rate input tax schemes (Arts. 28 and 29 MWSTG) for specific trades; (iv) no US check-the-box classification regime applies and hybrid mismatch outcomes follow the mandatory Swiss BEPS Action 2 implementing rules without elective carve-outs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG/LTVA), administered by the ESTV; bonded warehouse operations additionally fall under customs supervision of the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG) without constituting a separate local sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual turnover derived from taxable supplies and services in Switzerland and abroad (Art. 10(1) MWSTG); the threshold excludes exempt supplies, reverse-charge items and pure financing transactions; foreign-situs turnover is included when the business activity has a Swiss nexus through supplies of goods or services performed in Switzerland.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping exists in Switzerland. Invoicing must comply with Art. 26 MWSTG content requirements (seller and recipient identification incl. UID, date, type and scope of supply, consideration and VAT rate); the Swiss QR-bill (payment slip with QR code) is the mandatory settlement standard for domestic invoice payment traffic; electronic invoices in standardized XML or PDF format are accepted and retained for the statutory 10-year VAT record-keeping period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods qualifies for zero-rating (exemption with input VAT deduction) under Art. 23(1)(1) MWSTG when goods are physically transported from Switzerland to a foreign destination or into a foreign customs territory, including removal from an authorized Swiss bonded warehouse, in which case the customs outbound declaration must prove the removal has not occurred for Swiss domestic consumption; wines and spirits may be zero-rated only if the bonded goods are directly re-exported under customs supervision, and services directly benefiting those exports are likewise zero-rated when rendered to the foreign purchaser (Art. 23(1)(2)-(3)).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) processed in the Swiss electronic customs system e-dec or the EU NCTS export system with validated export reference number
Commercial invoice, purchase contract and bonded-transfer order identifying the foreign buyer and warehouse departure record (Lagerabmeldung)
Transport documents evidencing physical border-crossing (CMR waybill, bill of lading, air waybill or rail consignment note including foreign customs stamps or electronic arrival confirmation)
Bonded warehouse authorization number and warehouse outbound/seal record showing the goods left the customs warehouse under transit or re-export procedure
Inward foreign exchange remittance certificate (Swift wire or bonded-transfer settlement advice) from the Swiss payment bank proving settlement of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, missing, false, backdated or fraudulent export evidence triggers retroactive reclassification of the supply as taxable at 8.1%, with arrears plus default interest of 5% per annum (Art. 84 MWSTG) and disallowance of related input VAT deduction; intentional VAT evasion carries fines up to CHF 400,000, negligent evasion fines up to CHF 100,000 (Arts. 197-198 MWSTG), plus criminal seizure of unjust enrichment; recovery claims remain subject to a 5-year general assessment limitation, extended to 10 years where objective or intentional evasion is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank), Börsenstrasse 15, CH-8022 Zurich and Bundesplatz 1, CH-3003 Bern.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Switzerland imposes no exchange-control legislation, no capital-repatriation restrictions, and no prior approval requirement for inbound or outbound cross-border payments. Dividend and profit remittance to foreign shareholders is unrestricted provided corporate-law solvency requirements under Art. 680 CO are satisfied and Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) is duly declared and paid. For the newly incorporated Aktiengesellschaft, the capital-injection minimum is CHF 100,000 total nominal capital with at least CHF 50,000 paid in, being 20% of the nominal value of each issued share, pursuant to Art. 632 CO.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. The SNB does not impose surrender, conversion, repatriation timelines, or mandatory conversion ratios for export proceeds. The bonded-trade entity may retain EUR, GBP, and USD receipts in foreign-currency accounts indefinitely. The sole regulatory duty is statistical: Swiss residents must declare cross-border payment transactions to the SNB when monthly payment totals exceed CHF 10 million or when the number of declared individual transactions exceeds 25, in accordance with the SNB Payment Transactions Statistics Ordinance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (CHF/EUR/GBP/USD) for trade settlements and FX execution
Capital escrow account (share-capital verification) plus operational cash management
Operational trade account with documentary collections and letter-of-credit desk
Operational account for domestic payables, duty payments, and cash pooling
Custody and wealth-management account; less suitable for operational trade cash flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for FINMA-licensed Swiss fintechs; Low for foreign or offshore digital EMIs used as primary settlement accounts. Under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act (Fintech Licence), entities such as Yapeal, Neon, and Alpian may accept client deposits up to CHF 1 million with a lighter authorisation, but none offers the full documentary trade, excise-settlement, and customs-guarantee suite required for a bonded wine and spirits wholesaler. The EU/UK EMI passport does not extend into Switzerland; a foreign EMI operating as a principal clearing account would constitute unlicensed deposit-taking under FINMA practice. Recommended architecture: a Swiss-licensed commercial bank as the sole settlement spine, with a FINMA-regulated payment-technology layer or white-label API used solely for treasury automation and FX execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in the substantial majority of cases. For a newly incorporated AG with 100% foreign shareholders operating in the enhanced-risk alcohol trade, the Swiss Bankers Association Due Diligence Convention (CDB 20) and the identification provisions of FINMA's Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance require the bank to identify all beneficial owners and authorised signatories. In practice, UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank, and the cantonal banks insist on an in-branch interview with at least one UBO and one individual signatory holding individual signature authority. Purely remote account opening is accepted only for regulated financial intermediaries or existing low-risk clients under a narrow carve-out; it is not realistic for this entity. Budget five to eight business days in Switzerland for bank interviews, notarisation, commercial-register follow-up, and Federal Customs and Border Security Office (BAZG) excise-licence interviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent upstream ownership, including offshore entities, trusts, or foundations layered above the AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholders' register; full CDB 20 beneficial-ownership disclosure down to natural persons; apostilled certificate of good standing for each intermediate entity; source-of-wealth memorandum; certified passports of all UBOs and signatories; board-approved group organigramme; and a written treasury mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alcohol and bonded-warehouse classification giving rise to smuggling, excise-fraud, and sanctions trade-risk scenarios.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid excise and customs licence issued by BAZG; excise-suspension regime attestation; warehouse lease and storage insurance; verified supplier and buyer licences; stock-flow accounting records; municipal alcohol trade permit; physical inventory evidence; and an independent third-party audit report on the bonded operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate distribution of profits or high-value intra-group treasury activity in the first financial year.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited balance sheet demonstrating distributable reserves; legal opinion under Art. 680 CO; cash-flow projection and dividend policy; intercompany loan agreements at arm's length; Swiss tax clearance and debt-status confirmation from the cantonal tax authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large shareholder loan or third-party financing commingled with trade payables, creating unclear fund provenance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan and subordination agreements; counterparty KYC packs; arm's-length interest-rate benchmark memorandum; scheduled repayment plan; and board resolutions authorising each financing line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions-list, or adverse-media hits affecting a UBO or trade counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent adverse-media search results; PEP self-declaration; sanctions screening report covering OFAC, SECO, EU, and UN lists; transaction filtering evidence; and, where required, a compliance opinion letter coupled with contractual exclusion of sanctioned goods and persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute via SWIFT MT103 with the AG's capital escrow account as beneficiary, or via domestic SIC RTGS transfer in CHF; EUR tranches may arrive through euroSIC or SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 pain.001. The remittance information must carry the SNB payment-statistics purpose code applicable to non-trade capital transactions and the explicit wording 'Statutory share capital contribution'. The receiving bank verifies that at least CHF 50,000 or 20% of the nominal value of each issued share is unencumbered and blocks the funds until the commercial register confirms incorporation. Release to operations is conditioned on fulfilment of the treasury mandate and activation of the BAZG customs and excise licences.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for invoice settlement under open account or documentary collection, with Field 70 referencing the underlying contract, invoice number, and Incoterms; (2) commercial letters of credit issued by the Swiss relationship bank under UCP 600, sight or usance up to 90 or 180 days, with the bonded warehouse named as consignee or applicant for customs transit; (3) SEPA Credit Transfers for EU and EEA suppliers in the Bordeaux and Scotch corridors via euroSIC with full IBAN and BIC validation; (4) Swiss customs and excise payables settled by direct debit on the BAZG duty account; (5) excise-suspension dispatches within the EU documented under EMCS without border cash clearing, with customs guarantees collateralised on the operational trade account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF) up to 12 months, executed with a Swiss-regulated bank under an ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement.
European-style FX options (calls and puts) for hedging forecast trade flows, with premium paid upfront and no speculative leverage.
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF) for tenor-matched rebalancing of bonded-warehouse payment obligations.
Cross-currency basis swaps (XCCY) where long-term structural exposure arises from foreign-currency capital injections or refinancing.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to non-convertible currency legs such as USD/CNY or USD/INR; CHF NDFs are unavailable because the Swiss franc is freely deliverable, and any NDF referencing a CHF leg is treated as a synthetic instrument requiring full regulatory capital treatment.
OTC FX options cleared through SIX x-clear or an authorised broker, subject to a written treasury mandate and a non-speculative hedge ratio not exceeding 80% of forecast trade flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income & Capital Tax Return (profit tax, cantonal and communal taxes, including annual financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (seat canton) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for 31 December balance sheet date); extensions to 31 December are available upon written application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum on unpaid taxes; late-filing fines up to CHF 10,000; surcharge for tax evasion up to three times the tax evaded and criminal fines per Art. 174/175 Federal Tax Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return (periodic settlement for per XML/ELM portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filing period: by 31 March of the following year; for quarterly filers: within 60 days after end of each quarterly period (annual reconciliation attached to final quarter return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% on unpaid VAT, renewed monthly; interest at 4.5% p.a.; administrative fines up to 30% of the evaded VAT for willful omissions; criminal sanctions for tax fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employers' Wage Declaration and Social Security Report (AHV/UVG/EO/ALV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Equalization Fund (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) and Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office (FSIO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the year following the wage year; electronic submission via SUVA-Gateway by 28 February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compensatory interest of 5% per annum on undelivered contributions; administrative fines up to CHF 20,000 under Art. 89 AHV Act; criminal penalties for misrepresentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Bonded Warehouse Stock Inventory and Customs Declaration (Wines & Spirits under customs suspensive procedure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG), Civilian Customs Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Physical inventory as at 31 December; submission by 28 February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate duty and VAT assessment at full commercial rate; administrative fine up to CHF 10,000; suspension or revocation of bonded warehouse license; penal proceedings for irregularities per Art. 116 Customs Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Swiss mandatory ordinary audit if the company exceeds two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets > CHF 20 million; annual net turnover > CHF 40 million; annual average full-time employees > 250. Companies below these thresholds may undergo a limited audit (Review) or, if fewer than 10 full-time employees and unanimous shareholder consent, opt-out completely.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) Articles 957–963b; Swiss GAAP FER (Financial Reporting Standards) for small and medium-sized entities; IFRS permitted for individual statutory accounts and required for listed groups; no US GAAP in standalone statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not provide for a public annual UBO filing. The AG must maintain an internal Beneficial Owner Register in accordance with Art. 697l CO, updated upon any share transfer or change of control. The Board of Directors must verify and confirm the register's completeness at each Annual General Meeting; the register is presented to the Commercial Register Office or law enforcement upon official request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Board and General Meeting minutes)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (plus cantonal/communal direct taxes making the combined average effective rate generally 11%-21%; Zug and Zurich commonly at the lower end)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include: patent box regime (90% exempt qualifying IP income), R&D super-deduction up to 50% (i.e., total deduction of 150% of qualifying R&D expenditure), participation deduction eliminating 100% of qualifying dividend and capital gain income, and notional interest deduction on surplus equity in participating cantons. Additional relief may arise from tax treatment of holding companies, whether dormant or active, and from the absence of Swiss capital gains tax on private capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Eidgenössische Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration d'impôt fédéral pour les personnes morales), submitted electronically via the ESTV-recognized SwissTax XML interface or the competent canton’s eTax filing portal. The same annual return serves as the base for cantonal/communal taxes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the commercial fiscal year; cantonal tax authorities may grant extensions of up to an additional six months upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity of the Swiss AG: company name, registered office, UID/MWST number, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), date of incorporation, fiscal year start and end, and location of the bonded warehouse in Switzerland.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing entity is the Swiss-resident AG; foreign shareholders are not entered as Swiss taxpayers. Provide the ownership appendix listing non-resident shareholders by country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered shareholders with full names, addresses, percentage ownership, share par values, and date of any dividend resolution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach valid certificates of tax residence (TRC) for non-resident beneficial owners claiming DTA relief on dividends; the AG must identify the ultimate direct shareholder and any nominee arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Liquid funds, accounts receivable, bonded inventories of wine and spirits under customs supervision, non-bonded inventory, fixed assets, intangible assets, and intercompany loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose receivables and payables with foreign related parties and foreign related-party sales; the tax authority will screen these for hidden profit distribution risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2b / Balance sheet - liabilities and equity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, legal reserves, retained earnings, shareholder loans, bank debt, and other liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest-bearing shareholder loans from non-residents must be recorded accurately; excessive debt may be recharacterized as constructive equity, disallowing interest deductions and potentially causing deemed distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales of bonded wine/spirits and duty-paid domestic sales, cost of goods sold, warehousing and excise release costs, personnel expenses, depreciation, financial expenses, and other operating income/expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border sales to non-resident buyers at arm's-length prices; do not include excise duties or customs taxes as revenue; customs-bonded transfer documentation must match invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory add-backs (non-deductible expenses, hidden distributions, excessive partner/director compensation) and allowed deductions (participation deduction, patent box relief, R&D super-deduction, tax credit adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties or service fees paid to non-resident related parties require written agreements, real benefit testing, and TP documentation; absent substance they will be reclassified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4b / Withholding tax credits and foreign taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss federal withholding tax on Swiss-source dividend/interest income received by the AG, and foreign withholding taxes on foreign-source income for which treaty credit is claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include foreign taxes actually borne by the Swiss AG. The non-resident owner receives no credit in this return; recovery of Swiss WHT is a separate shareholder-level procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration that the return is correct and complete, with place, date, and signature of the chairman/CEO and, where applicable, the Swiss tax representative or licensed fiduciary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Swiss-resident director (or authorised Swiss representative) must sign; false declarations create personal criminal and civil liability for that signatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers reminder fees (typically CHF 100-500), disciplinary fines up to CHF 5,000, default assessment by estimation with a surcharge of 10%-33%, and interest on late tax. Intentional non-filing or false filing constitutes tax evasion subject to a penalty of 1.0-1.5 times the evaded federal tax, plus cantonal penalties; criminal prosecution may be initiated in serious cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on all Swiss-source dividend distributions to shareholders, irrespective of residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction; (2) submit the Swiss WHT reclaim/relief application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within three years after the end of the calendar year of distribution; and (3) attach the dividend payment confirmation, share register excerpt, and a beneficial ownership declaration. Under most Swiss DTAs, dividends to a 10%+ corporate shareholder are exempt or reduced to 0%-15%, provided the shareholder meets substance/anti-abuse requirements; refunds are made directly by ESTV after verification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss statutory withholding tax on IP royalties, and treaty rates are generally 0%. Debt interest: statutory Swiss WHT of 35% applies to interest on taxable bonds and bank deposits; under most Swiss DTAs the interest rate is reduced to 0% for beneficial owners such as banks or resident corporations, subject to TRC and anti-abuse review. Interest payments on pure intercompany loan balances without security-like documentation are generally outside the 35% WHT but remain subject to transfer pricing and anti-thin-capitalisation rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No explicit CHF statutory threshold for ordinary Local File/Master File; Swiss tax authorities expect contemporaneous arm's-length documentation whenever cross-border related-party transactions occur. Mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting applies to Swiss parent or subsidiary members of MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of CHF 900,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply zero-tax Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of offshore regimes. However, a Swiss AG engaged in bonded wine/spirits trade must maintain real physical presence, local management, employee capacity, and decision-making power in Switzerland. Otherwise the tax authorities may deny treaty benefits under beneficial ownership/limitation-on-benefits clauses, reclassify transactions, or challenge the entity as a letter-box company under Swiss abuse-of-law principles and anti-strip rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of taxable profit by omitting bonded warehouse sales, inflating costs, falsifying vintage stock valuations, or failing to declare duty-released sales as ordinary taxable revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 1.0-1.5 times the evaded federal tax plus accrued interest; cantonal penalties of similar magnitude; administrative default assessment and forfeiture of false storage records; in aggravated cases criminal proceedings under Swiss Criminal Code with fines and possible imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly approve false stock records are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax and penalties; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment (up to 3 years), confiscation of assets, and, for high-value cross-border schemes, travel bans and extradition matters.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or taxable bond/bank interest without deducting the 35% federal withholding tax and without obtaining an exemption or refund approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The debtor is personally liable to the Swiss tax authority for the un-withheld 35%; recovery interest and procedural fines apply; criminal sanctions for intentional failure can include fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly authorise gross distributions without WHT can be personally assessed as joint debtors for the withheld amounts; conviction under tax criminal law can impose monetary penalties and prison sentences on responsible officers, not just the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling bonded Scotch or Bordeaux wine to a foreign related importer below cost or above prevailing open-market price, or paying excessive management/royalty fees to a non-resident affiliate without substantive services or IP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax re-assessment at arm's-length prices, disallowance of expense deductions, reclassification of pricing differences as hidden dividends subject to 35% WHT, late interest, and penalties of 20%-40% of the tax adjustment; deliberate conduct escalates to evasion penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who set or approve non-arm's-length intercompany pricing with knowledge of tax consequence face personal joint and several liability for unpaid tax and WHT; criminal liability as accomplices to tax evasion may result in imprisonment and personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Swiss AG with no real business activity, no employees, and no bonded warehouse facility, used exclusively to route wine-trade profits and claim Swiss treaty benefits for non-resident owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA relief, retroactive refusal of Swiss WHT refunds, denial of tax residence status, reclassification of the entity as transparent, and recovery of all underpaid taxes plus interest and penalties; substantial economic taxes may be asserted on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors may be held personally liable for tax debts of a liquidated shell company under Swiss insolvency principles; criminal liability for fraudulent registration or false declarations can include imprisonment, travel bans, and disqualification from board positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Lack of Due Diligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or routing funds through the bonded wine/spirits trading entity with knowledge that the consideration originates from criminal activity, or processing payments for shell buyers, anonymity-preserving intermediary chains, or sanctions-exposed counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis punishes money laundering with imprisonment up to 3 years (or up to 5 years in qualifying cases) and a fine; Art. 305ter penalises negligent failure to verify beneficial owners with a fine up to CHF 500,000; asset confiscation is mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with actual or constructive knowledge of tainted funds face criminal conviction, extradition risk, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and exclusion from managing regulated entities; corporate veil-piercing exposes directors to civil restitution for amounts laundered through the AG.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bonded Warehouse and Excise Duty Diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Removing wine or spirits from bonded storage for domestic free circulation without customs release/excise payment, false declaration of alcohol strength or vintage age, or documentation fraud covering diverted consignments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full excise duty and VAT, forfeiture of goods, administrative fines up to three times the evaded duty, and criminal prosecution for customs/consumption tax evasion; duty suspension status is revoked and the licence may be cancelled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives of the licensed bonded warehouse operator are personally liable for the duty debt to the extent they directed or tolerated the diversion; criminal sentence can impose imprisonment for intentional smuggling or duty evasion, alongside personal confiscation of profits.
